S.source: printed p. 380; entry 'fazfaz'; sense 2; illustrates 'i–fazfaz'
S.FORM: huya wa shput i-fazfaz numa antu ma-shimzaw
S.PHON: huja wa ʃput ifaðfað numa antu maʃimðaw
S.FORM: huya wa shput i-fazfaz numa antu ma-shimzaw
S.PHON: huja βa ʃput iɸaðɸað numa antu maʃimðaw
S.TRANSL: That person is in the middle (so he) isn't cold

S.source: printed p. 380; entry 'fazfaz'; sense 3; illustrates 'ki–fazfaz'
S.TRANSL: You sit in the middle (the seat of honor)

S.source: printed p. 380; entry 'fazfaz'; sense 4; illustrates 'ma–i–fazfaz'
S.FORM: p-utu-i uan baruku ma-i-fazfaz a afu
S.PHON: putui uan baruku maifaðfað a afu
S.FORM: p-utu-i uan baruku ma-i-fazfaz a afu
S.PHON: putui uan baruku maiɸaðɸað a aɸu
S.TRANSL: Please fill the bowl half-way with rice

S.source: printed p. 380; entry 'fazfaz'; sense 4; illustrates 'ma–i–fazfaz'
S.FORM: shdu iza sa nak a baruku a afu ma-i-fazfaz
S.PHON: ʃdu iða sa nak a baruku a afu maifaðfað
S.FORM: shdu iza sa nak a baruku a afu ma-i-fazfaz
S.PHON: ʃdu iða sa nak a baruku a aɸu maiɸaðɸað
S.TRANSL: As for my bowl it can be half-full

S.source: printed p. 380; entry 'fazfaz'; sense 5; illustrates 'maka–fazfaz'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: or between two other people

S.TRANSL: He is sleeping in the middle of the bed

S.source: printed p. 380; entry 'fazfaz'; sense 6; illustrates 'ma–tana–fazfaz'
S.TRANSL: Midnight is upon us

S.source: printed p. 380; entry 'fazfaz'; sense 7; illustrates 'min–tana–fazfaz'
S.TRANSL: It's already midnight

S.source: printed p. 380; entry 'fazfaz'; sense 8; illustrates 'pan–na–fazfaz'
S.TRANSL: That person turned around in mid course

S.source: printed p. 380; entry 'fazfaz'; sense 8; illustrates 'pan–na–fazfaz'
S.TRANSL: I was going (and) turned back in mid-course

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'fazfaz' (opens on p. 380); sense 9; illustrates 'pi–fazfaz–in'
S.FORM: haya binanau'az pi-fazfaz-in maniun, numa ma-cuaw ma-qarman maqa antu ma-shimzaw
S.PHON: haja binanauʔað pifaðfaðin maniun numa maθuaw maqarman maqa antu maʃimðaw
S.FORM: haya binanau'az pi-fazfaz-in maniun, numa ma-thuaw ma-qarman maqa antu ma-shimzaw
S.PHON: haja binanauʔað piɸaðɸaðin maniun numa maθuaw maqarman maqa antu maʃimðaw
S.TRANSL: Put that woman between you (pl.), even though it's very bad, so she won't get cold

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'fciq'; illustrates 'fciq'
S.TRANSL: I'm afraid of a gun when it fires

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'fciq'; illustrates 'fciq'
S.TRANSL: The rice didn't sprout

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'fciq'; sense 2; illustrates 'fciq–an'
S.TRANSL: My vegetables (that I planted) have sprouted already

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'fciq'; sense 4; illustrates 'pa–fciq'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: with a gun, not an arrow

S.TRANSL: I shot a boar

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'fciq'; sense 5; illustrates 'p–in–a–fciq'
S.TRANSL: That gun was shot/detonated

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'fciq'; sense 6; illustrates 'p–in–a–fciq–an'
S.TRANSL: Someone shot this boar

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'fcu'; illustrates 'fcu'
S.FORM: nak a rima itia tusha wa fcu
S.PHON: nak a rima itia tuʃa wa fθu
S.FORM: nak a rima itia tusha wa fthu
S.PHON: nak a rima itia tuʃa βa ɸθu
S.TRANSL: My hand has two calluses

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'fcu'; sense 2; illustrates 'fcu–an'
S.FORM: nak a rima fcu-an maqa h-m-adu-hadu sa aqur
S.PHON: nak a rima fθuan maqa hmaduhadu sa aqur
S.FORM: nak a rima fthu-an maqa h-m-adu-hadu sa aqur
S.PHON: nak a rima ɸθuan maqa hmaduhadu sa aqur
S.TRANSL: My hands are callused from grasping a hoe habitually

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'fcu'; sense 3; illustrates 'f–in–c–fcu–an'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: but are not any longer

S.TRANSL: My hands were callused

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'fcu'; sense 3; illustrates 'f–in–c–fcu–an'
S.FORM: nak a rima f-in-c-fcu-an maqa miarain t-m-au-aqur sa buhat
S.PHON: nak a rima finθfθuan maqa miarain tmauaqur sa buhat
S.FORM: nak a rima f-in-th-fthu-an maqa miarain t-m-au-aqur sa buhat
S.PHON: nak a rima ɸinθɸθuan maqa miarain tmauaqur sa buhat
S.TRANSL: My hands used to be callused from always hoeing in the fields

S.source: printed p. 381; entry 'filhaq'; sense 5; illustrates 'maka–filhaq'
S.TRANSL: That tree is putting out leaves now

S.source: printed p. 382; entry 'filhaq' (opens on p. 381); sense 6; illustrates 'pu–filhaq'
S.FORM: ya mu-kaktun iza pu-filhaq, maka-bukay iza, numa cicu a bukay ma-qusu-qusum
S.PHON: ja mukaktun iða pufiɬaq makabukaj iða numa θiθu a bukaj maqusuqusum
S.FORM: ya mu-kaktun iza pu-filhaq, maka-bukay iza, numa thithu a bukay ma-qusu-qusum
S.PHON: ja mukaktun iða puɸiɬaq makabukaj iða numa θiθu a bukaj maqusuqusum
S.TRANSL: When it has finished putting out leaves, it blossoms, and its fruits are black

S.source: printed p. 382; entry 'filhaq' (opens on p. 381); sense 6; illustrates 'pu–filhaq'
S.FORM: numa sa ma-ra'in m-zai "dadú, ma-puzi-puzi a parakaz dai, numa ya pu-filhaq tata, sa caw mu-qca tish-hubuq la-tata"
S.PHON: numa sa maraʔin mðai dadu mapuðipuði a parakað dai numa ja pufiɬaq tata sa θaw muqθa tiʃhubuq latata
S.FORM: numa sa ma-ra'in m-zai "dadu, ma-puzi-puzi a parakaz dai, numa ya pu-filhaq tata, sa thaw mu-qtha tish-hubuq la-tata"
S.PHON: numa sa maraʔin mðai dadu mapuðipuði a parakað dai numa ja puɸiɬaq tata sa θaw muqθa tiʃhubuq latata

TRANSL.notes: Literal translation: one person is born again

S.TRANSL: Then the official said "It's true, when the white parakaz tree puts forth one leaf, another person is born"

S.source: printed p. 382; entry 'filhaq' (opens on p. 381); sense 7; illustrates 'qalha filhaq'
S.FORM: ma-cuaw ribush qalha filhaq, ma-qitan riqaz-an
S.PHON: maθuaw ribuʃ qaɬa fiɬaq maqitan riqaðan
S.FORM: ma-thuaw ribush qalha filhaq, ma-qitan riqaz-an
S.PHON: maθuaw ribuʃ qaɬa ɸiɬaq maqitan riqaðan
S.TRANSL: That plant has lots of leaves, and is pretty to see

S.source: printed p. 382; entry 'filhaq'; sense 4; illustrates 'mapa–filhaq'
S.TRANSL: Why are those two people spitting at each other

S.source: printed p. 382; entry 'filhaq'; sense 5; illustrates 'mat–filhaq'
S.FORM: yaku q-m-ig-ctu ma-sizaq, miarain yaku mat-filhaq
S.PHON: jaku qmiŋθtu masiðaq miarain jaku matfiɬaq
S.FORM: yaku q-m-ing-thtu ma-sizaq, miarain yaku mat-filhaq
S.PHON: jaku qmiŋθtu masiðaq miarain jaku matɸiɬaq
S.TRANSL: I ate something bitter (and) then I spit a lot

S.source: printed p. 382; entry 'filhaq'; sense 6; illustrates 'pa–filhaq'
S.TRANSL: Don't spit up phlegm!

S.source: printed p. 382; entry 'filhaq'; sense 6; illustrates 'pa–filhaq'
S.TRANSL: I want to spit

S.source: printed p. 382; entry 'filhaq'; sense 7; illustrates 'pash–filhaq–an'
S.TRANSL: Someone spit on my clothes

S.source: printed p. 382; entry 'filhish'; illustrates 'filhish'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: answer to What are you going to do?

S.TRANSL: Spread out the manure

S.source: printed p. 382; entry 'filhish'; sense 2; illustrates 'filhish–an'
S.FORM: yaku ya pishpirqit filhish-an sa pahat
S.PHON: jaku ja piʃpirqit fiɬiʃan sa pahat
S.FORM: yaku ya pishpirqit filhish-an sa pahat
S.PHON: jaku ja piʃpirqit ɸiɬiʃan sa pahat
S.TRANSL: When I transplant rice seedlings I spread out manure (for them)

S.source: printed p. 383; entry 'filhish' (opens on p. 382); sense 3; illustrates 'filhish–in'
S.FORM: numa a pa-tiklhun-an iza, filhish-in iza sa pahat
S.PHON: numa a patikɬunan iða fiɬiʃin iða sa pahat
S.FORM: numa a pa-tiklhun-an iza, filhish-in iza sa pahat
S.PHON: numa a patikɬunan iða ɸiɬiʃin iða sa pahat
S.TRANSL: When it was plowed the manure would be spread out

S.source: printed p. 383; entry 'finshiq'; illustrates 'finshiq'
S.TRANSL: They are sowing rice

S.source: printed p. 383; entry 'finshiq'; illustrates 'finshiq'
S.FORM: yaku sahala finshiq sa shaglaw, numa shashanu riqaz-ak min-dadu iza fciq iza
S.PHON: jaku sahala finʃiq sa ʃaŋlaw numa ʃaʃanu riqaðak mindadu iða fθiq iða

S.PHON: jaku sahala ɸinʃiq sa ʃaŋlaw numa ʃaʃanu riqaðak mindadu iða ɸθiq iða
S.TRANSL: The day before yesterday I planted vegetables (and) this morning I saw them sprouting

S.source: printed p. 383; entry 'finshiq'; sense 2; illustrates 'fa–finshiq'
S.TRANSL: She is sowing seed

S.source: printed p. 383; entry 'finshiq'; sense 3; illustrates 'f–in–inshiq'
S.TRANSL: The seed has been sown

S.source: printed p. 383; entry 'finshiq'; sense 3; illustrates 'f–in–inshiq'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: answer to Shi–ntua ihu? Where did you go?

S.TRANSL: I just sowed the rice

S.source: printed p. 383; entry 'finshiq'; sense 3; illustrates 'f–in–inshiq'; quoted in the translation of blust-ex-p0383-e006
S.TRANSL: Where did you go?

S.source: printed p. 383; entry 'finshiq'; sense 4; illustrates 'finshiq–an'
S.FORM: numa ya tan-lhuan iza pu-shuqish-in pu-sahay-in ma-ra'in a kaunu, numa finshiq-an sa qtilha, numa isisuaiza ia-naur-an k-m-an qca

S.FORM: numa ya tan-lhuan iza pu-shuqish-in pu-sahay-in ma-ra'in a kaunu, numa finshiq-an sa qtilha, numa isisuaiza ia-naur-an k-m-an qtha
S.PHON: numa ja tanɬuan iða puʃuqiʃin pusahajin maraʔin a kaunu numa ɸinʃiqan sa qtiɬa numa isisuaiða ianauran kman qθa

TRANSL.notes: Source note: the turnips being prepared for pickling

S.TRANSL: Then in the evening they would be returned to the big wooden trough, and sprinkled with salt, then when they were ready they would continue to crush them underfoot

S.source: printed p. 383; entry 'finshiq'; sense 5; illustrates 'finshiq–in'
S.TRANSL: She is sowing the paddy seed

S.source: printed p. 384; entry 'finshiq' (opens on p. 383); sense 7; illustrates 'pin–fa–finshiq–in'
S.TRANSL: This seed of the guava is used for planting

S.source: printed p. 384; entry 'firit'; sense 2; illustrates 'sh–in–u–firit'
S.FORM: ya sh-in-u-firit iza kalisian ya ma-qulha-qulha, ma-dishlum, shadunan
S.PHON: ja ʃinufirit iða kalisian ja maquɬaquɬa madiʃlum ʃadunan

S.PHON: ja ʃinuɸirit iða kalisian ja maquɬaquɬa madiʃlum ʃadunan

S.source: printed p. 384; entry 'firit'; sense 3; illustrates 'sh–m–u–firit'

S.source: printed p. 384; entry 'firit'; sense 3; illustrates 'sh–m–u–firit'

S.PHON: ʃmufirit jaku sa kɬiw a minhulus

S.PHON: ʃmuɸirit jaku sa kɬiw a minhulus

S.source: printed p. 384; entry 'firit'; sense 4; illustrates 'shu–firit'; reading 1 of 2 of 'ata (tu) shu–firit alushun'

S.source: printed p. 384; entry 'firit'; sense 4; illustrates 'shu–firit'; reading 2 of 2 of 'ata (tu) shu–firit alushun'

S.source: printed p. 385; entry 'fizin' (opens on p. 384); sense 5; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'maka–fizin'

S.TRANSL: I will go walking on a level surface

S.source: printed p. 385; entry 'fizin' (opens on p. 384); sense 7; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'man–fizin'; reading 2 of 2 of 'yaku a man–fizin/yaku a mun–saháy man–fizin'
S.TRANSL: I will go walking on a level surface

S.source: printed p. 385; entry 'fizin' (opens on p. 384); sense 8; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mapa–sha–fizin'

S.source: printed p. 385; entry 'fizin' (opens on p. 384); sense 9; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'masha–fizin'

S.source: printed p. 385; entry 'fizin' (opens on p. 384); sense 10; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mun–sa–fizin'

S.source: printed p. 385; entry 'fkat'; illustrates 'fkat'

S.PHON: bafkat iða na paniða ʃmuruʃuruð iða na rusaw

S.TRANSL: Wow! The fishing pole is dipping, let's pull up the fish!

S.source: printed p. 385; entry 'fkat'; sense 4; illustrates 'fkat–in'
S.TRANSL: Someone set off my noose trap

S.source: printed p. 385; entry 'fkat'; sense 5; illustrates 'mu–fkat'; reading 1 of 2 of 'yaku t–m–uqris, mu–fkat na tuqris, pish–qaqa/pish–raput'

S.FORM: yaku t-m-uqris, mu-fkat na tuqris, pish-qaqa

S.source: printed p. 385; entry 'fkat'; sense 5; illustrates 'mu–fkat'; reading 2 of 2 of 'yaku t–m–uqris, mu–fkat na tuqris, pish–qaqa/pish–raput'

S.FORM: yaku t-m-uqris, mu-fkat na tuqris, pish-raput

S.source: printed p. 385; entry 'fkat'; sense 5; illustrates 'mu–fkat'
S.FORM: yaku t-m-uqris takic, kan qca-n sa takic tuqris, mu-fkat m-ara iza sa takic
S.PHON: jaku tmuqris takiθ kan qθan sa takiθ tuqris mufkat mara iða sa takiθ

S.source: printed p. 385; entry 'fkat'; sense 6; illustrates 'pu–fkat–in'

S.PHON: takiθ ja mupapanaq iða ʃmufkat iða
S.FORM: takith ya mu-pa-panaq iza, sh-m-u-fkat iza
S.PHON: takiθ ja mupapanaq iða ʃmuɸkat iða
S.TRANSL: When a barking deer enters a trap the trap closes on it

S.source: printed p. 386; entry 'flhi'; illustrates 'flhi'

S.source: printed p. 386; entry 'flhi'; illustrates 'flhi'

S.source: printed p. 386; entry 'flhuq'; illustrates 'flhuq'

S.source: printed p. 386; entry 'flhuq'; illustrates 'flhuq'

S.source: printed p. 386; entry 'flhuq'; illustrates 'flhuq'

S.PHON: aðaðak maqa maɬaɬiqaʃ maradaradak sa but fɬuqan sa ina wa θiθu numa tu finɬuqan iða paʃiwanan sa hulus
S.FORM: azazak maqa malhalhiqash ma-rada-radak sa but, flhuq-an sa ina wa thithu, numa tu f-in-lhuq-an iza pashiwan-an sa hulus

S.TRANSL: Because he was playing the child got all dirty (so) his mother washed him, and when he was washed (she) changed his clothes

S.PHON: nak a hulus ɸinɬuqin nak a binanauʔað

S.source: printed p. 386; entry 'flhuq'; sense 7; illustrates 'flhu–flhuq–an'

S.source: printed p. 386; entry 'flhuq'; sense 7; illustrates 'flhu–flhuq–an'

S.FORM: haya wa fatu flhu-flhuq-an sa hulus

S.PHON: haja βa ɸatu ɸɬuɸɬuqan sa hulus
S.TRANSL: That stone is a place where clothes are washed

S.source: printed p. 386; entry 'flhuq'; sense 8; illustrates 'flhuq–an'
S.TRANSL: You washed my back

S.source: printed p. 386; entry 'flhuq'; sense 8; illustrates 'flhuq–an'
S.TRANSL: My wife washed me

S.source: printed p. 386; entry 'flhuq'; sense 9; illustrates 'flhuq–i'

S.source: printed p. 387; entry 'flhuq' (opens on p. 386); sense 10; illustrates 'flhuq–in'

S.source: printed p. 387; entry 'fqat'; illustrates 'fqat'

S.source: printed p. 387; entry 'fqat'; sense 4; illustrates 'fqat–in'

S.FORM: tu thaw a taun kahiwan yanan sa kufulh-an sa tafulh, numa kufulh-an sa lhimza, numa ya uka sa lhimza k-m-ilhim sa qris ta-fqat-an thaythuy, numa ma-baza-bazay kufulh thaythuy sa taun
S.PHON: tu θaw a taun kahiβan janan sa kuɸuɬan sa taɸuɬ numa kuɸuɬan sa ɬimða numa ja uka sa ɬimða kmiɬim sa qris taɸqatan θajθuj numa mabaðabaðaj kuɸuɬ θajθuj sa taun
S.TRANSL: The old-style Thao houses were roofed with miscanthus or sword grass, but if sword grass wasn't available slabs of slate were split off and when they were thin they were used to roof the house

S.source: printed p. 387; entry 'fqat'; sense 6; illustrates 't–m–a–fqat'

S.source: printed p. 388; entry 'fuar' (opens on p. 387); illustrates 'fuar'

S.TRANSL: The baby chick has hatched

S.PHON: ranaw a qariθuj a ɸuθikan iða ja simaq a matabraq iða

S.source: printed p. 388; entry 'fuczash'; sense 1a; illustrates 'fuczash a afu'

S.source: printed p. 389; entry 'fuilh'; illustrates 'fuilh'

S.PHON: ani iðahaj maraʔin tu ɸinuiɬ jakin a masakup

S.PHON: ja kariʃkiʃ ɸuiɸuiɬ mita βa lalaβa

S.PHON: haja ʃput mimbuqnur maqa fuiɬak maqa ihu mumuqmuq maɬinuna

S.PHON: haja ʃput mimbuqnur maqa ɸuiɬak maqa ihu mumuqmuq maɬinuna

S.source: printed p. 389; entry 'fuilh'; sense 4; illustrates 'fuilh–ak'

S.PHON: fuiɬi wak ja muŋkuða sa saran ja a munaj
S.FORM: fuilh-i wak ya mung-kuza sa saran ya a mu-nay
S.PHON: ɸuiɬi βak ja muŋkuða sa saran ja a munaj

S.source: printed p. 390; entry 'fuilh' (opens on p. 389); sense 6; illustrates 'fuilh–i'

S.PHON: fuiɬi uan dai juhu mita wa lalawa
S.FORM: fuilh-i uan dai yuhu m-ita wa lalawa
S.PHON: ɸuiɬi uan dai juhu mita βa lalaβa

S.source: printed p. 390; entry 'fukish'; sense 2; illustrates 'k–m–ashi–fukish'

S.PHON: ihu ja mapaθaj sa mihu a binanauʔað kmaʃiɸukiʃ mihu a binanauʔað

S.source: printed p. 390; entry 'fukish'; sense 3; illustrates 'mapa–kashi–fukish'

S.PHON: binanauʔað masa binanauʔað ja mapaθaj mapakaʃiɸukiʃ

S.source: printed p. 390; entry 'fulhashi'; sense 2; illustrates 'lhum–fulhashi'

S.PHON: nak a rima miarain tmauaqur ɬumfuɬaʃi sa rima

S.PHON: nak a rima miarain tmauaqur ɬumɸuɬaʃi sa rima

S.source: printed p. 390; entry 'fulhashi'; sense 2; illustrates 'lhum–fulhashi'

S.source: printed p. 390; entry 'funfun'; illustrates 'funfun'
S.TRANSL: Squirrels often eat the fruit of the funfun tree

S.source: printed p. 390; entry 'funuq'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ish–funuq'
S.FORM: huya wa binanau'az m-ara diplhaq na bantac, ish-funuq painan, numa ma-da-diplhaq na bantac
S.PHON: huja wa binanauʔað mara dipɬaq na bantaθ iʃfunuq painan numa madadipɬaq na bantaθ

S.PHON: huja βa binanauʔað mara dipɬaq na bantaθ iʃɸunuq painan numa madadipɬaq na bantaθ

S.source: printed p. 391; entry 'funuq' (opens on p. 390); sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ma–funuq'

S.source: printed p. 391; entry 'funuq' (opens on p. 390); sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ma–funuq ma–funuq'
S.FORM: haya wa buhat ma-cuaw ma-funuq qalha pruq, numa ma-funuq

S.TRANSL: Those fields are well prepared for planting

S.source: printed p. 391; entry 'funuq' (opens on p. 390); sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ma–funuq'
